title: Agent Install Manifest
description: Schema for the ecosystem-wide agentic install contract manifest. Each repo in a dependency chain declares its own direct deps, install entry-points, and functional probes at this contracted path. Spec: docs/wiki/agent-install-contract.md (canonical source: coordinator/docs/wiki/agent-install-contract.md in the DoE-claude clone; published mirror at ~/.claude/plugins/coordinator/docs/wiki/agent-install-contract.md).

shared_interpreter_surface.description: Names this repo claims in an interpreter it does NOT own exclusively. Every entry is a name no sibling repo can also claim, so the block exists to make collisions inventoriable from the manifest rather than discoverable only by reading each repo's packaging. Optional: omit it when the repo installs into its own venv and claims nothing shared. An EMPTY block is not the same as an absent one -- it asserts the surface was considered and is empty.

top_level_import_names.description: Importable top-level module/package names claimed on sys.path.

console_scripts.description: Executable names placed on PATH by this install.

entry_point_groups.description: Entry points registered per group, e.g. {"project_rag.addons": ["market_intel"]}.

sys_path_entries.description: Paths added to sys.path outside normal site-packages resolution.

install_mechanism.description: How the claim is made, e.g. "pep660-editable-finder". Free text: the mechanism vocabulary is not fixed fleet-wide, and an enum here would refuse manifests for mechanisms nobody has met yet.

startup_cost_ms.description: Import cost this claim adds to an interpreter that loads it.

startup_cost_measured.description: REQUIRED whenever startup_cost_ms is present, and the reason this pair is two fields rather than one. A declared estimate and a measured number render identically once written down, and budgets get built on whichever landed.

agent_install_contract_version.description: Contract version — enables coordinated schema bumps across repos. Consumers must reject manifests with a version they do not recognise. Readers accept the range {1,2,3} (reader-widen-first sequencing) so manifests at different versions can coexist during a coordinated bump; v2 adds the optional DirectDep.consumer_install_args field; v3 adds the optional system_prerequisites array; v3 also adds the optional programmatic_entry_point field.

repo_id.description: Canonical repo identifier (matches the GitHub repository name). Used as the visited-set entry key during chain-walk.

setup_skill.description: The slash-command that a human types to invoke the agentic setup flow (informational — not the agent dispatch primitive; see agent-install-contract.md §Skill chain-walker).

doctor_skill.description: OPTIONAL. The slash-command that a human types to invoke a doctor/health-check flow (informational). Omitted entirely by repos that have no health-check flow — not every conforming repo warrants one (e.g. a research-pipeline plugin). Avoid the bare name `doctor`/`/doctor` even when present: it collides with Claude Code's native `/doctor` on bare-name resolution; name any real health command distinctly (e.g. `/coordinator:code-health`).

standalone_setup_script.description: Paths to the standalone (non-skill) setup scripts, relative to the repo root. This is the chain-walk DAG dispatch target — the script the chain-walker invokes when walking dependency chains. `entry_point_contract` (optional) describes the chain-walk invocation contract for `posix`/`windows` above, and doubles as the Point-2 FALLBACK witness — authoritative only when the top-level `programmatic_entry_point` field is absent (see that field's `entry_point_contract.description` for the in-band precedence rule). The agentic setup skill (`setup_skill`) stays a human wrapper that delegates to `posix`/`windows` here; no install logic lives only in the skill.

posix.description: Relative path to the POSIX (bash) standalone setup script.

windows.description: Relative path to the Windows (PowerShell) standalone setup script.

entry_point_contract.description: OPTIONAL. Declares that `posix`/`windows` above form a single non-interactive, flag-driven, deterministic-exit-code chain-walk invocation. This is the Point-2 FALLBACK witness: authoritative only when the top-level `programmatic_entry_point` field is absent from this manifest. When `programmatic_entry_point` is present, that field's `entry_point_contract` is the authoritative Point-2 witness instead — see its description for the verbatim precedence rule.

programmatic_entry_point.description: OPTIONAL. A dedicated, purpose-built programmatic install entry point — distinct from `standalone_setup_script` (the chain-walk DAG dispatch target). When present, this is the PREFERRED Point-2 witness for packageability contract point 2. Shape mirrors `standalone_setup_script`: `posix` (required), `windows` (optional — no assumption that a Windows twin exists), and an optional `entry_point_contract` describing the non-interactive/check-only/deterministic-exit contract.

posix.description: Relative path to the POSIX (bash) programmatic entry point script.

windows.description: OPTIONAL. Relative path to the Windows (PowerShell) programmatic entry point script.

entry_point_contract.description: OPTIONAL. Packageability contract point 2 — declares that `posix`/`windows` above form a single non-interactive, flag-driven, deterministic-exit-code install/register/assemble command. This is the PREFERRED Point-2 witness. In-band precedence rule: When both programmatic_entry_point.entry_point_contract and standalone_setup_script.entry_point_contract are present, programmatic_entry_point is the authoritative Point-2 witness; standalone_setup_script.entry_point_contract describes only the chain-walk invocation and is the Point-2 fallback only when programmatic_entry_point is absent.

direct_deps.description: Ordered list of direct upstream dependencies. The chain-walker processes these in declaration order. Does not include transitive deps — each upstream declares its own.

required_env_vars.description: Environment variables that must be set for this repo's install to succeed. The standalone script prompts for any that are missing in interactive mode and fails fast in non-interactive mode.

required_local_surfaces.description: OPTIONAL. Registrations written INTO the operator's ~/.claude (or other configurable_locations root) that a `git pull` cannot carry -- distinct from `required_mcp_surfaces` (marketplace plugins / external MCP servers) and `required_env_vars` (shell environment). Each entry must be re-performed on every machine; when it isn't, a session on that machine is silently missing the capability with no signal, since every other install-surface check measures a repo artifact. Reuses the McpSurface vocabulary (`id`, `description`, `why`, `tier`, `probe`, `install`, `reference`) rather than inventing a parallel one.

override_flags.description: The canonical flag-pair that bypasses the hard-dep consent gate. Both flags must be passed together; passing only one produces exit code 93.

skip_dep_check.description: Flag string that signals the caller explicitly intends to skip dependency checking.

accept_hallucination_risk.description: Flag string that signals the caller explicitly accepts the hallucination risk of running without all hard deps.

system_prerequisites.description: OPTIONAL. Machine-level system prerequisites probed at Step Zero before any install proceeds. `cmd` is the universal probe every consumer resolves; `ref` is a fast-path valid ONLY for verbatim-vendors of prereq_probe.sh and MUST NOT be relied on by non-vendors. `tier` is the ENV-PREREQ-PROBE taxonomy (hard|semi-hard|advisory mirrored from step-zero-emitter-contract.md § severity Enum); it is ORTHOGONAL to `direct_deps[].severity` (the manifest-dep taxonomy hard|soft|optional in agent-install-contract.md § Severity semantics). Distinct JSON paths; shared `hard`/`semi-hard` spellings are intentional alignment with the emitter, not aliasing. Canonical shape settled by DR-INSTALL-002 (central is the canonical-shape owner; DAG-root contract-minting authority).

provider_capabilities.description: OPTIONAL. Declares the repo's role in the install DAG and its refresh/hoist capabilities. Only the DAG root (coordinator-claude) declares role 'upstream-provider'. Downstream consumers omit this field or declare role 'consumer'. Enables the chain-walker to early-hoist provider setup at Step Zero before processing consumer deps. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-06-24-install-baton-completeness-claude-code-validation.md § Upstream-provider early-hoist.

role.description: DAG role of this repo in the install chain. 'upstream-provider' = DAG root that other repos depend on; 'consumer' = a repo that depends on an upstream provider.

plugin_self_registration.description: When true, this repo registers its own plugin during install (self-contained plugin activation). The chain-walker can skip the registration step for dependencies that set this true.

refresh_primitive.description: Relative path (from this repo root) to the script that refreshes the live-install copy of this plugin. Empty string when the repo relies on an upstream refresh primitive rather than owning one.

hoistable_at_step_zero.description: When true, the chain-walker may hoist this provider's setup to Step Zero (before processing any consumer deps). Enables early-hoist for DAG roots whose setup is a prerequisite for all downstream install steps.

installer_floor.description: OPTIONAL. Packageability contract point 3 (installer-floor split). A BOUNDARY ANNOTATION, not a re-declaration — the floor itself (git, the Claude Code CLI) is already expressed as `system_prerequisites` entries with `id: git` / `id: claude_code`; this field cross-references those ids rather than restating their probe/install shape. The only genuinely novel content here is `install_root_drivable`. An external provisioner (e.g. Example-os-repo) is expected to provision the floor; this repo declares deps ABOVE that line.

floor_prerequisite_ids.description: Ids of the `system_prerequisites` entries (e.g. ["git", "claude_code"]) that constitute the floor this repo assumes an external provisioner has already supplied. Each id MUST match a `system_prerequisites[].id` declared elsewhere in this manifest — do not restate the prereq's probe/install/reference here.

install_root_drivable.description: When true, this repo's install is drivable against an externally-provided install root and carries no hardcoded assumption of `~/.claude` or a fixed sibling-dir layout. When false, the repo has a known hardcoded-path limitation above the floor.

tested_platforms.description: OPTIONAL. Packageability contract point 4 (real, declared, tested platform support). Distinguishes platforms this repo's entry point has been executed-and-verified on (`tested_platforms`) from platforms it merely ships code for (`present_platforms`, e.g. a static-reviewed-only PowerShell twin). A platform absent from `tested_platforms` MUST NOT be marketed as supported parity even if present in `present_platforms`.

present_platforms.description: OPTIONAL. Packageability contract point 4 — platforms for which this repo ships an entry-point implementation (e.g. a `.ps1` twin) without execution verification. See `tested_platforms` for the executed-and-verified subset.

configurable_locations.description: OPTIONAL. Packageability contract point 6 — every configurable location this repo resolves (install root, projects root, package store, data root, dep/sibling roots, etc.), expressed as a detect → suggest → default → override surface rather than agent-only instructions. Vocabulary follows the machine-local-registry.md § 4 resolution ladder: discovery.candidates are ranked rungs (env/flag → tracked search-roots autodiscovery → tracked path-exceptions → registry.local.toml last-resort). Override is a unified `{flag, env}` vocabulary (at least one required); dep/sibling-root locations (`dependency_id` present) are a first-class location-class and require BOTH flag and env — the per-dep override is the load-bearing knob, a single-install-root derivation is admissible only as a subordinate default candidate.

packageability_compliance.description: OPTIONAL opt-in compliance marker for the fleet packageability contract (docs/wiki/agent-install-contract.md § Packageability). `validate-install-contract.py` keys its completeness checks on `declared === true` — a v3 manifest that omits this field, or sets `declared: false`, SKIPS CLEAN (no packageability checks fire). Presence with `declared: true` is the positive signal that this manifest intends to be checked against points 1/2/3/4/6.

declared.description: True once this repo has opted this manifest in to packageability-contract completeness checking.

required_mcp_surfaces.description: OPTIONAL. MCP-served capabilities this repo's agents depend on, distinct from `system_prerequisites` (machine-level binaries) and `direct_deps` (sibling repos). Two kinds share this array via the `kind` discriminator rather than two parallel top-level fields: `plugin` — a Claude Code marketplace plugin gated by `settings.json` `enabledPlugins`; `external_server` — an externally-installed MCP server the user installs and self-registers. Additive, reader-first (same precedent as `provider_capabilities` — no contract version bump).

EntryPointContract.description: Shared non-interactive/check-only/deterministic-exit contract shape referenced by both `standalone_setup_script.properties.entry_point_contract` and `programmatic_entry_point.properties.entry_point_contract` — each call site overrides this def's description with its own parent-level precedence-rule text (2020-12 permits `description` as a sibling annotation alongside `$ref`).

non_interactive_flag.description: OPTIONAL. Flag string that runs the entry point with no interactive prompts (e.g. '--non-interactive', '--i-am-agent').

check_only_flag.description: OPTIONAL. Flag string that runs the entry point in dry-run/check mode — reports what would change without mutating state.

deterministic_exit.description: OPTIONAL. When true, the entry point's exit code is a deterministic, documented contract (not merely zero-on-success/nonzero-on-failure by accident) that callers can branch on.

SystemPrereq.description: A single machine-level system prerequisite — a tool or capability that must exist on the machine before install can proceed.

id.description: Canonical probe identifier, e.g. 'git', 'python', 'gh'. Matches the probe function suffix in prereq_probe.sh where a ref function exists.

tier.description: ENV-PREREQ-PROBE severity tier (DR-INSTALL-002 settled enum). hard = block install. semi-hard = warn loudly, offer remediation, continue only with confirmation (this is the 'soft-but-important / escapable-with-flag' case). advisory = warn, never block. The pre-DR `optional` value was retired — it carried no distinct semantic vs `advisory`.

probe.description: Probe definition. Reuses the FunctionalProbe `kind`+`cmd` shape (DR-INSTALL-002). `kind` is required (system-prereq probes are presence checks — `command_succeeds`); auth/liveness is verified by setup scripts + doctor probes, not collapsed into the manifest probe. `ref` is a fast-path to a _co_probe_<id> function in prereq_probe.sh and is valid ONLY for verbatim-vendors of that lib.

kind.description: Probe kind, reusing the FunctionalProbe enum vocabulary (DR-INSTALL-002 §2c). System prerequisites are presence probes — `command_succeeds` in practice.

cmd.description: Universal shell command to check for the prerequisite. Must be portable (sh-compatible). E.g. 'command -v git'.

shell.description: OPTIONAL (DR-INSTALL-002 §2c, ratified from ue-addon). When true, the probe `cmd` must run through a shell rather than as a bare exec.

ref.description: OPTIONAL. Names a _co_probe_<id> function in the vendored prereq_probe.sh lib. A vendor-only fast-path — MUST NOT be relied on by non-vendors of prereq_probe.sh.

windows.description: OPTIONAL. Windows-native probe command, mirroring `install.windows`'s posix/windows split (DR-INSTALL-002 §2d precedent). Runs natively on Windows (`where.exe <name>` or a PowerShell one-liner) instead of relying on `cmd`'s POSIX-shell idiom (`command -v`, `||`, `test`), which is not runnable as declared outside WSL/Git-Bash. Additive and optional — `cmd` stays the unconditionally-required universal leg so a windows-less entry never strands POSIX consumers. Absent `windows`, a runner MUST fall back to `cmd`.

windows_shell.description: OPTIONAL. Mirrors `shell` but governs the `windows` leg only. When true, `windows` is a PowerShell command run via `powershell -NoProfile -Command "<windows>"` (or `pwsh` where available) rather than a bare exec such as `where.exe`. Defaults to `false` (bare exec) when omitted.

install.description: Install instructions for a human or agent when the prerequisite is missing. Shape settled by DR-INSTALL-002 §2d: `mode` is required; `posix`/`windows` carry per-platform install command strings (load-bearing for `auto-with-confirmation`); `remediation` carries the one-line human instruction for `manual`. Both auto and manual entries validate under this additive shape.
install.$comment: DR-INSTALL-002 settled this shape as ADDITIVE — the cross-field dependency (auto-with-confirmation SHOULD carry posix/windows; manual SHOULD carry remediation) is a RUNTIME emitter responsibility, intentionally NOT schema-enforced via allOf. A mode-only entry validates clean. Do not add conditional enforcement without re-ratifying the DR — it would reject already-shipped consumer entries.

mode.description: Install mode (DR-INSTALL-002). 'auto-with-confirmation' = first-class automated install with a printed confirmation + opt-out (encoded by the literal string); the per-platform `posix`/`windows` command strings supply what runs. 'manual' = the operator installs it themselves; `remediation` carries the instruction, no automated path is provided.

posix.description: OPTIONAL. POSIX (sh/bash) install command string, run on confirmation under `mode: auto-with-confirmation`.

windows.description: OPTIONAL. Windows (PowerShell) install command string, run on confirmation under `mode: auto-with-confirmation`.

remediation.description: OPTIONAL (required in spirit for `mode: manual`). One-line human-readable install instruction. May reference per-OS package managers.

applies_to.description: OPTIONAL (DR-INSTALL-002 §2e, ratified from ue-addon). Which install class(es) this prerequisite applies to. Defaults to ["consumer"] when omitted.
applies_to.$comment: `default` is a metadata annotation per JSON Schema 2020-12 — a standard validator does NOT inject it into instance data. Runtime consumers MUST apply the ["consumer"] default themselves when the key is absent.

reference.description: REQUIRED (DR-INSTALL-002 §3 required item keys). Doc pointer — path or URL to further documentation about this prerequisite.

DirectDep.description: A single direct upstream dependency declaration. NOTE: coordinator-claude's own chain-walker (coordinator_core.ops.setup_chain_walker.dep_probe, claude-klabauter) reads FLAT functional_probe_kind/functional_probe_args fields, not a nested functional_probe object -- this sub-schema was corrected 2026-07-19 (W0.5 Option B+C) to match that ACTUAL parser, which is the authoritative shape for coordinator's own manifest. Distinct from SystemPrereq.probe (nested {kind, cmd}), which is a separate, unrelated field consumed by a different probe path.

id.description: Canonical dependency identifier (matches the upstream's repo_id).

severity.description: How the chain-walker treats a missing or broken instance of this dep. hard = block unless override flag pair + double-confirm. soft = warn loudly, offer to walk chain, proceed if user declines. optional = offer once, no warning if declined.

sibling_dir_name.description: Expected directory name of the sibling clone, relative to the consumer repo's parent directory. The chain-walker checks for sibling presence at <parent>/<sibling_dir_name> before running the functional probe -- EXCEPT for the claude_klabauter_seam_resolvable probe kind, which bypasses the sibling check entirely (registry/env-resolved dep, not sibling-directory-colocated). Still required by this schema for uniformity; the walker ignores its value for that one probe kind.

upstream_url.description: Canonical GitHub HTTPS URL for cloning this dep.

functional_probe_kind.description: Probe kind. sibling_dir_exists: implicit always-run check, no additional fields. file_exists: functional_probe_args.path required. python_import: functional_probe_args.expr required. command_succeeds: functional_probe_args.cmd required. claude_klabauter_seam_resolvable: no additional fields -- bypasses the sibling_dir_exists gate and confirms via a live find_spec("coordinator_core.invoke") check (added W0.5 Option B+C for the claude-klabauter dep, which is registry/env-resolved, not sibling-colocated).

functional_probe_args.description: OPTIONAL. Kind-specific probe arguments: {"path": ...} for file_exists, {"expr": ...} for python_import, {"cmd": ...} for command_succeeds. Omitted (or empty object) for sibling_dir_exists and claude_klabauter_seam_resolvable, which take no arguments.

consumer_install_args.description: Optional. Args the CONSUMER wants passed to this upstream's standalone setup script (install mode + version selection). Composed by the chain-walker with --i-am-agent and the UPSTREAM's override_flags; does NOT include the upstream's override flags (those are read from the upstream manifest — see override_flags). Introduced in contract v2; intentionally NOT version-guarded — a v1 manifest carrying this field validates clean, consistent with the reader-widen-first doctrine.

distribution.description: OPTIONAL. How a consumer actually obtains this dep when `upstream_url` alone would mislead — e.g. a private repo whose URL 404s for anyone without access. `private-access-on-request` flags that case: the maintainer grants access on request rather than the repo being publicly cloneable. Absent entirely for deps where a plain `git clone` of `upstream_url` just works. Not version-guarded, same reader-widen-first rationale as `consumer_install_args`.

distribution_note.description: OPTIONAL. Short human-readable elaboration of `distribution` — required in practice whenever `distribution` is present, but not schema-enforced as a pair to keep the two fields independently optional.

FunctionalProbe.description: A probe that verifies the dep is not only present but functional. Supplements the implicit sibling_dir_exists check.

kind.description: Probe kind. sibling_dir_exists: implicit always-run check, no additional fields. file_exists: requires path. python_import: requires expr. command_succeeds: requires cmd.

remediation.description: OPTIONAL. Packageability contract point 1 — what to do when this probe fails. Reuses the SystemPrereq.install shape (`mode: auto-with-confirmation` with per-OS `posix`/`windows` commands, or `mode: website` with a `url` for un-scriptable prerequisites like the Epic launcher or git-for-windows). Distinct from `SystemPrereq.install` only in $ref location — same settled shape.

path.description: File path to check for existence, relative to the sibling repo root.

expr.description: Python import expression to evaluate via the resolved Python interpreter. Must succeed (exit 0) for the dep to be considered functional.

cmd.description: Shell command to execute. Must exit zero for the dep to be considered functional. Escape hatch for non-Python upstreams.

FunctionalProbe.$comment: unevaluatedProperties at THIS level per JSON Schema 2020-12 spec — properties evaluated by adjacent in-place applicators (the if/then chain in allOf) and by this object's own `properties` declaration count as evaluated; extra fields outside both are rejected.

Remediation.description: Packageability contract point 1 remediation shape — deliberately a SEPARATE def from SystemPrereq.install (which is DR-INSTALL-002-settled and not to be restructured here). Either a machine-runnable command (`mode: auto-with-confirmation`, per-OS `posix`/`windows`) or a website URL for the un-scriptable class (Epic launcher, git-for-windows) via `mode: website`.

mode.description: 'auto-with-confirmation' = first-class automated remediation with a printed confirmation + opt-out; the per-platform `posix`/`windows` command strings supply what runs. 'website' = the prerequisite has no scriptable install path — `url` points a human at the installer download page.

posix.description: OPTIONAL. POSIX (sh/bash) remediation command string, run on confirmation under `mode: auto-with-confirmation`.

windows.description: OPTIONAL. Windows (PowerShell) remediation command string, run on confirmation under `mode: auto-with-confirmation`.

url.description: OPTIONAL (required in spirit for `mode: website`). Website URL a human follows to install the un-scriptable prerequisite (e.g. the Epic Games launcher, git-for-windows).

PlatformId.description: Canonical platform identifier vocabulary shared by tested_platforms and present_platforms (packageability contract point 4).

ConfigurableLocation.description: Packageability contract point 6 — one configurable location this repo resolves, expressed as detect → suggest → default → override rather than agent-only instructions. Vocabulary follows the machine-local-registry.md § 4 resolution ladder (env/flag → tracked search-roots autodiscovery → tracked path-exceptions → registry.local.toml last-resort). Covers both single-repo locations (install root, projects root, package store, data root) and dep/sibling-root locations (`dependency_id` present) — the latter a first-class location-class per the 2026-07-11 claude-klabauter point-6 ruling. Override is a single unified `{flag, env}` vocabulary; a dep-root location's override MUST carry both (the per-dep knob is load-bearing), never a parallel top-level `root_override` object.

name.description: Identifier for this configurable location, e.g. 'install_root', 'projects_root', 'ue_root', 'package_store', 'data_root'.

dependency_id.description: Present IFF this location is a sibling/dependency root — the id of the dependency repo whose root this resolves (e.g. 'coordinator-claude'). A dependency-root location's override MUST carry both a flag and an env (the per-dep knob is load-bearing); its default is a subordinate sibling derivation, admissible only as a rung-2 default candidate, never the sole knob.

discovery.description: How this repo discovers candidate paths for this location — yields RANKED candidates, not a found/not-found boolean.

candidates.description: Ranked discovery rungs, most-preferred first, using the machine-local-registry.md § 4 ladder vocabulary (e.g. 'tracked search-roots autodiscovery via marketplace.json marker', 'tracked path-exceptions table', 'registry.local.toml last-resort fallback').

default.description: Sane default path (or path-deriving rule) used when no candidate is confirmed, so the install flow can proceed silently.

override.description: How a human/GUI (e.g. Example-os-repo) injects an explicit path for this location, bypassing discovery/default. Unified vocabulary: a flag and/or an env var. At least one is required. A dependency-root location (dependency_id present) requires BOTH — the per-dep override is the load-bearing knob per the 2026-07-11 claude-klabauter point-6 ruling.

ConfigurableLocation.$comment: This allOf's then.properties.override.required:[flag,env] composes with the base override.anyOf (line ~491, MAY-either) per 2020-12 in-place applicator semantics — both constraints apply to the same override sub-schema, so a dependency_id-bearing location ends up MUST-both while a plain location stays MAY-either. Not orphaned/no-op despite override having no re-declared `type` in the then branch (code-reviewer Finding 4, verified correct).

McpSurface.description: A single required MCP-served capability — a marketplace plugin or an externally-installed MCP server that coordinator's agents depend on. Reuses the `tier` vocabulary from `SystemPrereq` (hard|semi-hard|advisory), not a fresh severity enum.

id.description: Canonical identifier for this MCP surface, e.g. 'context7', 'notebooklm-mcp'.

kind.description: 'plugin' = a Claude Code marketplace plugin enabled via settings.json enabledPlugins, self-registering its MCP server. 'external_server' = an externally-installed tool the user installs and self-registers as an MCP server (not marketplace-distributed).

tier.description: Same ENV-PREREQ-PROBE tier vocabulary as SystemPrereq.tier. Both surfaces currently declared here are semi-hard: absent, they degrade dependent agents/pipelines to a guessing or unavailable state rather than blocking install outright.

description.description: What this surface is — plugin/package identity, the MCP server name it serves, and its tool-name prefix.

why.description: Why coordinator needs this surface — names the specific degraded agents or pipeline, not a generic 'improves quality' claim.

probe.description: Detection probe. json_object_key_true reads a JSON file at `relative_path` under the `configurable_locations` entry named by `location`, and passes only when the object at `json_path` carries `key` with a truthy value. Both legs are required: `enabledPlugins` is an object keyed by 'name@marketplace' whose values are booleans, so a bare key-presence check reports an explicitly-disabled plugin as enabled. Reads JSON rather than shelling out to grep, so it stays cross-platform. command_succeeds reuses the SystemPrereq.probe convention for a CLI-presence check.

location.description: REQUIRED for json_object_key_true. Names an entry in this manifest's own `configurable_locations` (e.g. 'install_root') whose discovery ladder resolves the directory. A named reference, not an interpolated path token — this manifest defines no token-substitution contract, and one probe does not justify minting it.

relative_path.description: REQUIRED for json_object_key_true. Path to the JSON file, relative to the directory `location` resolves to, e.g. 'settings.json'.

json_path.description: REQUIRED for json_object_key_true. Top-level key in the file whose value is the object to look up in, e.g. 'enabledPlugins'.

key.description: REQUIRED for json_object_key_true. The key that must be present in the object at `json_path` with a truthy value for the probe to pass.

cmd.description: REQUIRED for command_succeeds. Universal probe command, e.g. 'command -v nlm'. Cross-field requirement (kind-specific fields) is a runtime emitter responsibility, same convention as SystemPrereq.install — not schema-enforced via allOf, per DR-INSTALL-002 §2d precedent.

shell.description: OPTIONAL, for command_succeeds. Same semantics as SystemPrereq.probe.shell — when true, `cmd` must run through a shell rather than as a bare exec.

windows.description: OPTIONAL, for command_succeeds. Same semantics as SystemPrereq.probe.windows — a Windows-native probe command, falling back to `cmd` when absent.

windows_shell.description: OPTIONAL, for command_succeeds. Same semantics as SystemPrereq.probe.windows_shell — governs the `windows` leg only.

install.description: Install/enable instructions. Same shape as SystemPrereq.install.

reference.description: Doc pointer — path to further documentation about this surface.

LocalSurface.description: A single required machine-local registration -- state written into the operator's install root (e.g. ~/.claude/settings.json) that a `git pull` cannot carry, so it must be re-performed on every machine. Reuses the `tier` vocabulary from `SystemPrereq`/`McpSurface` (hard|semi-hard|advisory), not a fresh severity enum.

id.description: Canonical identifier for this local surface, e.g. 'statusline-registration'.

description.description: What this surface is -- the registration's shape and where it lives on disk.

why.description: Why coordinator needs this surface -- names the specific degraded consumer or capability, not a generic 'improves quality' claim.

tier.description: Same ENV-PREREQ-PROBE tier vocabulary as SystemPrereq.tier / McpSurface.tier.

probe.description: Detection probe. json_key_present reads a JSON file at `relative_path` under the `configurable_locations` entry named by `location`, and passes only when the top-level key at `json_path` resolves to a non-null value. json_object_key_true reuses the McpSurface probe of the same kind -- reads the object at `json_path` and passes only when `key` inside it is truthy. Both stay zero-subprocess: a file read and a JSON parse, never a shell command -- see the boot-path zero-spawn mandate in coordinator/hooks/scripts/project-orientation.py's module docstring, which is the consumer of this probe shape. A `command_succeeds`-kind probe is deliberately NOT admitted here (unlike McpSurface.probe, which allows it) -- the boot-path consumer cannot spawn a subprocess to evaluate one, and it would be declared only to be silently skipped.

location.description: REQUIRED. Names an entry in this manifest's own `configurable_locations` (e.g. 'install_root') whose discovery ladder resolves the directory. A named reference, not an interpolated path token.

relative_path.description: REQUIRED. Path to the JSON file, relative to the directory `location` resolves to, e.g. 'settings.json'.

json_path.description: REQUIRED. Top-level key to resolve in the file -- for json_key_present, the key whose value must be non-null; for json_object_key_true, the key whose value is the object to look up `key` in.

key.description: REQUIRED for json_object_key_true. The key that must be present in the object at `json_path` with a truthy value for the probe to pass. Not used by json_key_present.

install.description: Install/register instructions. Same shape as SystemPrereq.install / McpSurface.install, except `remediation` is REQUIRED here (unlike its siblings): the boot-path banner in project-orientation.py skips any entry lacking a non-empty `remediation` string, so a schema-valid entry without one would silently never surface -- the declared-but-unevaluable gap this manifest section exists to prevent, one level deeper than probe.kind.

reference.description: Doc pointer — path to further documentation about this surface.
